data.long_meaning: From the Greek word amethystos, meaning 'not intoxicated'. In ancient Greece, amethyst was believed to protect against intoxication and was used as a symbol of sobriety and piety. The name Amathiste carries the meaning “Amethyst gemstone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Amathiste usually hope their child will grow to embody amethyst gemstone and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.long_meaning: A female Christian name of geographical origin, such as Amathiste, referring to Jewish settlements in Asia Minor. It is derived from the name of the city Amathus in Cyprus, which was a major center of Jewish influence in the region. In Christian tradition, the name Amathiste symbolizes the connection between the faith and the cultural heritage of the ancient world. People with this name are often associated with qualities such as adaptability, resilience, and a strong sense of community.
